Ramp Developer API overview

## Overview

Permanent link: Overview

Ramp’s Developer API allows teams to programmatically access Ramp data and build automations or integrations tailored to their workflows. It provides secure, scoped access to objects like transactions, cards, users, and more. This help article explains what the API is, how to get started within the Ramp app, and where to find full technical documentation and real-time assistance. Complete reference guides, endpoint schemas, and end-to-end examples live in the Ramp Developer API documentation↗.

## Setup guide and feature support

Permanent link: Setup guide and feature support

To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.

Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead. See Publish an app for other Ramp businesses.

  1. Open Developer apps↗ in Ramp.
  2. For your first app, click Start building. If you already have an app, click Create new app.
  3. Name your app (e.g., “API Quickstart”) and accept the Terms.
  4. Under Grant types, confirm Client credentials is turned on.
  5. Under Scopes, click Configure allowed scopes and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as `transactions:read`. If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access.
  6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securely—you’ll need them to generate your access token.

Video walkthrough: Generate Ramp Developer API credentials from the Ramp dashboard. Best when you're creating your first app and need client credentials and scopes. Watch the video↗.

Once credentials are created, follow the this guide on how to generate an access token↗.

## Sandbox environment

Permanent link: Sandbox environment

Ramp provides a sandbox environment where you can build and test your API integration before connecting to production. The sandbox is a separate environment with its own base URL and credentials — it is not a mode within the production API.

  * Sandbox API base URL: `https://demo-api.ramp.com`
  * Production API base URL: `https://api.ramp.com`

The sandbox uses a separate API base URL and app credentials from production. It cannot process real money and includes demo-only simulation actions.

### Requesting sandbox access

Permanent link: Requesting sandbox access

Request access using the sandbox access form↗. Your sandbox should be ready in about one minute. Check your inbox for an account access email. Ramp provisions a sandbox business pre-populated with sample data (such as transactions, cards, users, departments, and reimbursements) so you can test against realistic data without affecting your production account.

You will need to create a separate developer app in the sandbox environment to obtain sandbox-specific OAuth2 credentials (Client ID and Client Secret). Follow the same setup steps described in Setup Guide and Feature Support above, but within your sandbox account.

### Sandbox vs. production

Permanent link: Sandbox vs. production

  * Use the API for your own Ramp business: Create a separate developer app in your production Ramp account and send production requests to `https://api.ramp.com`.
  * Build for other Ramp businesses: Test your integration in sandbox. When you are ready, publish your app from the Developer console.
     * Already have access: Skip this step.
     * Need access to your company's existing Developer console, including when your invite expired: Ask the person who received your company's invite, or another admin on that console, to invite you. Don't submit another application. If no one can invite you, see How to contact Ramp's Support team.
  2. Sign in with your Developer console account and open the Developer console↗.
  3. Open your app. To use an existing app, select its row in the app list. To create one, click Start building for your first app, or New app if you already have one. Enter an App name, accept the Developer Terms of Service, and click Create app.
  4. On your app's Production access tab, click Apply, then complete the application. If you already started an application, the tab shows its status:
     * Complete your application: Click Complete application to finish it.
     * Application requires attention: Check your email for Ramp's feedback, then click Edit application to update it. If you haven't received an email, contact partnerships@ramp.com.
     * Application submitted: awaiting review: No action is needed. Ramp emails you with updates.
  5. After Ramp approves your production access application, onboard production customers through OAuth.

Advisor Console partners: If Ramp gave you a separate embedded partnership application link, submit that application in step 1 instead. After Ramp approves it, the invite adds you to Advisor Console instead of a Developer console. Use the Advisor Console developer settings↗ for steps 2–4 instead of the Developer console link. Only Console admins can open these settings. To give a teammate access, invite them↗ as a Console admin, or, if they're already a member, select them on the People↗ tab and change their role to Console admin. Console admins can also invite people, access all client accounts, and change others' roles, so review Advisor Console roles and permissions before granting it.

Apply appears only when no role in your Developer console business can sign in with a password. If the tab says SSO or SAML login must be enabled, click Configure and turn off Password for each role in sign-in controls, then return to the tab to click Apply.

> Important: Before you turn off Password for a role, confirm that everyone with that role can sign in with SSO or SAML. Otherwise, they can't sign in.

If you still can't open the Developer console with your Developer console account, see How to contact Ramp's Support team.

## How to submit a developer API support ticket

Permanent link: How to submit a developer API support ticket

  1. Open Developer apps↗:

Image: Company navigation with Developer highlighted

  2. Click Developer API Support.

  3. In Ask Ramp, describe your issue and ask to connect with the Developer Support team:

Image: Ask Ramp new chat with generic suggested questions

  4. Review the pre-filled Description, enter a Subject, and add any other missing details:

Image: Developer Support ticket form with an empty Subject and a pre-filled Description

  5. Click Submit Ticket to send your request to the team:

Image: Submit Ticket button at the bottom of the support ticket form

## Developer assist

Permanent link: Developer assist

Developer Assist is an AI-powered helper built directly into the Ramp API documentation. It can answer questions about endpoints, parameters, errors, and implementation steps in real time.

To use it:

  1. Navigate to the Ramp Developer API docs.
  2. Click the chat icon in the bottom-right corner of the page.
  3. Type your question into the chat window to get instant guidance.

Video walkthrough: Test Ramp Developer API calls and manage scopes for your integration. Best when validating your setup or refining permissions for an existing integration. Watch the video↗.

For bug investigations or issues with API performance or unexpected behavior, submit a Developer API support ticket.

# 

Quickstart

Copy Markdown

* * *

  * 1. Create your app and get credentials
  * 2. Get an access token
  * 3. Make your first API call

This guide will help you make your first Ramp API call in just a few minutes. You'll create an access token and call the Transactions API to retrieve transaction data.

This guide assumes you are a Ramp customer with admin access to your dashboard. Need a test environment for development? Request sandbox access.

## 1. Create your app and get credentials

Permanent link: 1. Create your app and get credentials

First, you'll need to create a developer app to get your API credentials.

  1. In your Ramp account, go to Company → Developer (you'll need admin access).
  2. Click Create New App.
  3. Name your app (e.g., "API Quickstart") and accept the Terms.
  4. Under Grant types, click Add new grant type → select Client Credentials.
  5. Under Scopes, click Configure allowed scopes and select `transactions:read`.
  6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store them securely – you'll need them in the next step.

For more details on authorization, see the Authorization Guide.

## 2. Get an access token

Permanent link: 2. Get an access token

With your credentials, request an access token. Ramp authenticates this `/developer/v1/token` request with HTTP Basic Auth: base64-encode `client_id:client_secret` and send it in the `Authorization` header. The token authenticates your API requests.

Replace `{environment-url}` with:

  * `https://demo-api.ramp.com` for Sandbox
  * `https://api.ramp.com` for Production

## 

API URLs are different from the Ramp app URLs

The API base URL is not the same as the URL for the Ramp customer app. Make sure you're pointing your API calls at the API host, not the frontend host.

Environment  | API base URL  | Ramp app URL
--- | --- | ---
Production  | `https://api.ramp.com`  | `https://app.ramp.com`
Sandbox (demo)  | `https://demo-api.ramp.com`  | `https://demo.ramp.com`

## IT Admins

Permanent link: IT Admins

IT Admin is a base role for employees who need to manage integrations, provisioning, and account security on Ramp. IT Admins have the same permissions as an Employee with additional access to People, Company Settings, Developer API, and Integrations.

Best for: IT teams, developers.

IT Admins can:

  * Manage user provisioning and account security settings
  * Configure integrations and Developer API access
  * Edit People and Company Settings
  * Use Ramp cards and funds issued to them (same as Employee)

IT Admins cannot:

  * View or manage expenses or transactions
  * Access Bill Pay
  * Access accounting integrations (unless customized on Plus)

> Note: Administrators can assign IT Admins additional manager permissions. For more details, see Editing a user's role.

For more details on this role, see IT Admin.

## View-Only Admins

Permanent link: View-Only Admins

View-Only Admin does not require Ramp Plus. It is not available with standalone Bill Pay access alone.

# Logging into Ramp for the first time

## Overview

To sign in to Ramp for the first time, you need an invite from a Ramp admin, Business Owner, or manager at your company. The invite email contains a secure link that takes you to the Ramp signup page, where you create your account using the sign-in method your company has configured.

This article covers how to accept your invite, what sign-in options you may see, and what to do if something goes wrong.

## Accept your invite

  1. Open the invite email from Ramp and select the secure invite link.
  2. You will see a Claim your account page showing that your company has invited you to join Ramp.
  3. Create your account using the sign-in method shown on screen. Depending on your company's settings, you may see email and password fields, a Create account with Google button, a Claim with SSO button, or a combination of these options.
  4. Use the same email address that your company used to invite you.

If you already have a Ramp account with another business, Ramp will recognize your email and ask you to sign in to your existing account first.

# 

Authorization

Before using the API, you'll need to set up authorization. To quickly get started, refer to our Setup Guide.

## Create a token

Permanent link: Create a token

Expects two headers:

  * Authorization header formed from base-64 encoded client credentials as `Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>`
  * `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

Required content body depends on authorization type method, as defined by `grant_type`.

  * Authorization Code Grant (`grant_type=authorization_code`): `grant_type`, `code`, and `redirect_uri` are required. Request must happen after requested scopes have been approved and exchanged for authorization code.
  * Refresh Token Grant (`grant_type=refresh_token`): `grant_type` and `refresh_token` are required. User must have previously obtained refresh token in authorization code flow.
  * Client Credentials Grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`): `grant_type` is required. If `scope` is omitted, the access token has no scopes.

User role deep-dive: IT Admin

## Overview

Permanent link: Overview

The IT Admin is a user role for employees, typically IT teams or developers, who need to manage integrations, provisioning, and account security on Ramp. IT Admins do not have access to the business's spend information and cannot manage spend controls. IT Admins have the same permissions as an employee or cardholder with additional access to edit People, Company Settings, Developer API, and Integrations.

> Note: The IT Admin role is available across all Ramp business types, including the Ramp Accounts Payable Product Bundle (AP-only experience).

IT Admins are the direct counterpart to Finance Admins. While Finance Admins manage financial products (expenses, Bill Pay, accounting, treasury), IT Admins focus on user management, integrations, SSO/security, and the Developer API. Together, these roles represent the two most comprehensive areas of administration within Ramp.
